Messages.Author: Peter Oh
Messages.Body:
"Eric Schultheis" <phee...@netwiz.net> wrote in message
news:3D63BA27...@netwiz.net...

> If I am a longtime player, and am only looking to collect the new cards
> do I need to buy the new Camarilla Edition starter sets? If all the new
> cards are in the CE boosters then I would probably be better off buying
> only boosters.
>
> I searched all over for a clear answer, and couldn't find one.

If you are primarily concerned with getting the 100 new vampires in the set
and the 15 new library cards, then yes, spending your money on Boosters is
the way to go. All of the new cards are in there. The main incentive for
the veteran player to buy the precon starter decks is to make it a certainty
that you will get some reprints that were previously very difficult to
obtain such as Freak Drives, 2nd Traditions, and Disarms.

Hope that's clear enough.

Peteo

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
Eric Schultheis wrote:

> If I am a longtime player, and am only looking to collect the new cards
> do I need to buy the new Camarilla Edition starter sets? If all the new
> cards are in the CE boosters then I would probably be better off buying
> only boosters.

There are no new cards in the starters that aren't in the boosters. On the
other hand, each starter comes with 7 or 8 reprinted vampires (reprints from
AH and DS, generally) that have the new background and design, and sometimes
new art (for instance, in the Nosferatu starter, you get Nikolaus and
Daliyah, both of whom come with new pictures). So if you are looking just
for playable new cards, then you don't need any starters. If you are looking
for a complete set of something, then you'll need one of each starter.

That, and the Starters come with some really good, old cards (Ventrue gives
you *two* Freak Drives; Brujah gives you a Disarm).
